response: Read the guidance and select the representation, conversion and verification required by each case.

cases.input: Write a new project-owned receipt instant, with no prescribed consumer format, at 2026-10-05T15:58:05.123456789Z.
cases.acceptance: Use an explicit UTC ISO 8601 instant retaining all required fractional precision; do not reduce it to whole seconds or milliseconds.

cases.input: Create a new UTC timestamp filename where colons are prohibited and no other spelling is required.
cases.acceptance: Use the ISO 8601 basic UTC form with T and Z, preserving any required precision. Do not rename existing supported identifiers.

cases.input: A Cargo source-cache manifest requires epoch nanoseconds, and an archive consumer prescribes numeric timestamps.
cases.acceptance: Keep the numeric formats and required units. Verify exact values, precision and supported range rather than imposing ISO text on the consumer.

cases.input: Display the instant 2026-10-06T01:30:00Z to a user whose configured timezone is America/Toronto.
cases.acceptance: Write 2026-10-05T21:30:00-04:00 or an equivalent EDT rendering. Convert the calendar date as well as the clock time.

cases.input: Store the calendar date 2026-10-05 and an elapsed duration of 90 seconds.
cases.acceptance: Keep the date date-only without adding midnight or a timezone; keep the duration as an elapsed amount in its required representation and units.

cases.input: Convert a local date-time during a daylight-saving overlap into an instant, but the contract supplies no zone or ambiguity resolution.
cases.acceptance: Do not invent an offset or silently choose one occurrence. Obtain the required zone and resolution from the contract or supplied context before conversion.

cases.input: A user requests UTC timestamps in a report; its machine-readable receipt already uses UTC.
cases.acceptance: Honor the request for the report and preserve UTC machine records. The normal local-time rule does not override an explicit user request.

cases.input: An external tool requires its timestamp grammar and existing Git refs already contain tool-owned date identifiers.
cases.acceptance: Preserve those consumer formats and existing identifiers. The rule does not authorize protocol changes or identifier renames.
